subject: Clarify hybrid-context billing and seat-credit conversion
messages:
From: Sarah White <sarah@acmeretail.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: purchasing@acmeretail.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Billing question: hybrid traffic (streaming + sessions) and seat credits

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked great. Before we move to procurement, we need one last clarification from finance: how does Redwood bill when a single customer uses a mix of streaming endpoints (low-latency one-off responses) and long-lived multi-turn sessions (chat with KV cache)? Specifically:

- Do requests from streaming endpoints get aggregated with session traffic for the purposes of the minimum/billing quantum?
- How does Redwood round partial token usage across those two patterns?
- Our procurement team is evaluating whether our reserved seats can be converted to token credits on a monthly basis; can you share the exact conversion formula and any rounding rules?

We have a pilot next month and need an official statement for our PO. Attaching our expected usage profile (small sample).

Thanks,
Sarah White
VP Product, Acme Retail
Attachments: usage-sample.csv
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah White <sarah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing question: hybrid traffic (streaming + sessions) and seat credits

Sarah — great questions. TL;DR: we keep aggregation consistent at the account-model level and apply a single billing quantum per model variant; seat credits are converted to a monthly token allowance using a deterministic formula and a small rounding floor. Details below and I attached a worked example (billing-example.xlsx).

1) Aggregation boundary
- We aggregate usage at the account + model family + region level. Streaming calls and session calls that target the same model variant will roll up into the same usage bucket for the billing window (hourly aggregation that feeds the daily invoice). This prevents double-charging when customers split patterns across endpoints.

2) Billing quantum & rounding
- Billing quantum: 32-token granularity for base models, 16-token for distilled variants (when enabled).
- Aggregation window: usage is aggregated per 1-hour window and rounded up to the nearest quantum within that window. Example: if in one hour you consume 1,345 tokens on model X, we round to ceiling(1345 / 32) * 32 = 1,376 tokens for billing.
- Cross-pattern mixing: streaming vs session are both included in the same per-hour tally for the model variant; we do not apply separate quanta for the two patterns.

3) Seat credit conversion
- Formula: monthly_token_credit = seat_count * seat_multiplier * standard_monthly_hours
- Where: seat_multiplier = 220,000 tokens per seat (this is our canonical conversion for the Redwood Standard seat) and standard_monthly_hours = 720 (used to pro-rate for partial months). In short, 1 seat = 220,000 tokens/month.
- Rounding: after computing monthly_token_credit we apply a final rounding to the nearest 1,000 tokens (banker's rounding). We do this to keep invoice line items tidy for large contracts.

4) Minimums & exceptions
- Per-account minimum floor: if an account's total billed tokens for a month fall below 10,000 tokens after seat conversion, we apply a 10,000-token minimum (this is to cover fixed infra).
- Exception process: for pilots with predictable low-volume bursts we can set a temporary floor at 5,000 tokens for up to 2 months; exceptions must be requested in writing (sales + finance sign-off).

I'll loop in Marissa (billing) and Rishi (pricing) to confirm the seat_multiplier for enterprise vs pilot SKUs. Attached is the worked example that maps your sample usage into billed lines.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: billing-example.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Billing question: hybrid traffic (streaming + sessions) and seat credits

Forwarding to Billing + Legal for visibility. Quick notes:
- For enterprise SKUs we actually use seat_multiplier = 250,000 tokens/seat (higher than the public list) when customers buy committed seats as a URC (usage-reservable commitment).
- The 32-token quantum is correct for our primary q8 quantization path; some custom quantized models (customer-managed) may use a 64-token quantum if kernel fusion prevents fine-grained accounting — we surface that up-front in the MPA.
- On rounding: finance prefers rounding to the nearest 500 tokens instead of 1,000 for mid-sized deals; we can propose 500 for ACME and document it in the SOW.

Action: Rishi/Monica, can you confirm a recommended proposal (seat_multiplier + rounding) for a pilot that converts to a 12-month committed seat contract? We should also include the temporary 5k pilot floor and be explicit about the hour-based aggregation window.

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Aditya/Marissa — thanks, this helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups before we issue the PO:

- Please confirm the seat_multiplier you recommend for a 3-month pilot (we want to understand conversion if we convert to 12 months).
- Can you add the exact wording for the 5k pilot floor exception so procurement can include it in the PO?
- Any limits on mixing model variants? For example, if we use a distilled variant for streaming and a full model for session history, will those be billed separately?

If you can send a short one-page statement (PDF) that we can attach to the PO, procurement will be able to push this through quickly.

Best,
Sarah
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah White <sarah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing question: hybrid traffic (streaming + sessions) and seat credits

Sarah — great. Proposal we can sign off on for the pilot (I will follow up with a PDF and DocuSign link):

1) Pilot seat_multiplier: 220,000 tokens/seat for the 3-month pilot conversion. If ACME converts to a 12-month committed seat contract within the pilot window, we will apply a conversion uplift to 250,000 tokens/seat for the remainder of the committed term.

2) Pilot floor wording (for PO): "Redwood will apply a pilot billing floor of 5,000 billed tokens per month for the duration of the pilot (maximum two consecutive months). This pilot floor will be superseded by any subsequent committed seat agreement."

3) Mixing model variants: Billing is by model variant. If you call a distilled variant for streaming and a full variant for session traffic, each variant is tallied independently and rounded per the quantum associated with that variant (typically 16-token quantum for distilled, 32-token for full). If you pin a single variant across endpoints we aggregate into a single bucket. We will include a short table in the PDF that lists quanta by variant.

4) Rounding proposal for ACME: round to nearest 500 tokens on monthly invoice lines (instead of the default 1,000). We'll lock this in the SOW for ACME pilot.

Next steps: I will generate the one-page confirmation and DocuSign the pilot SOW. If everything looks good we can have procurement sign by EOD Monday.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
